experiment: MOAT-003 GREEN — Generic HTTP Bearer Authority
requirements: A supported operation-level OpenAPI HTTP bearer requirement remains discoverable as a capability.
RIGHTCLICK reflects only generic authority metadata and never the bearer secret.
The credential is looked up outside context_run through a macOS Keychain generic-password item.
Canonical authority origin lowercases scheme and host, removes default HTTP/HTTPS ports, and excludes path, query, and fragment.
Missing bearer authority returns unavailable with authority_unavailable evidence before any provider transport.
A credential bound to another origin must never be reused.
When exact authority is present, RIGHTCLICK injects Authorization: Bearer <secret> at the HTTP transport boundary.
The bearer secret must not appear in capability metadata, execution messages, execution events, provider output, or outcome evidence.
Unsupported security schemes, multiple alternatives, multiple simultaneous schemes, non-empty bearer scopes, and other unsupported security shapes abstain rather than guessing.
Root-level inherited security is not silently ignored. In this milestone it abstains unless an operation explicitly overrides it.
An explicit operation security: [] overrides root-level security and remains public.
Existing unauthenticated OpenAPI capabilities retain their current behavior.
Origin pinning and redirect protections remain unchanged.
No provider-specific or Cloudflare-specific behavior may be added.
No new MCP tool names may be added.
The existing context_run MCP input schema must remain unchanged.
The bearer secret must never be supplied as a context_run argument.
